gh issue create --title "A pause resumed after a suspend swallows the space bar and wants Enter instead" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

Suspend the game at `[HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]` and resume it, and the
space bar does nothing: the player has to press Enter before paging
continues. The next pause behaves normally.

## Why

`getch()` in `osx.c` puts the terminal into non-canonical, no-echo mode
with `tcsetattr()` and then blocks in `read()`. A stop and continue
leaves the terminal in canonical mode -- the shell restores what it
saved when it took the foreground back -- while the reader is still
blocked in the read it set up before the stop. In canonical mode the
line discipline holds the space until a newline arrives, so the read
does not return until Enter.

## Reproduced

Both modes, side by side at 80x24:

- plain (`sst` with no `-t`)
- `-t` fallen back to the classic display

Both swallow the space and both take Enter instead, so this is not
specific to the full-screen path or to anything curses does. A `-t` game
whose panels are **up** is unaffected: `tui_getch()` reads through
curses, which reinstates its own program mode on resume.

## Why it matters

Small, and recoverable without knowing anything -- pressing Enter works,
and most players would press something else and move on. It is worth
filing because the manual promises resizing is safe "while the game
waits for an answer or for a keystroke at a pause" and this is the
neighbouring gesture failing quietly, and because the reader is one
`tcsetattr()` away from being right.

## Where it was found

By `ui-review` on the branch for #158, which fixed a *different* suspend
defect: a fallback game could not be resumed at all, because
`endwin()` left curses' `SIGTSTP` handler installed. That is fixed and
this is what is left. Explicitly not caused by it -- plain mode, which
that change does not touch, behaves identically -- so it was filed
rather than folded in.

## Fixing it

`getch()` could re-apply its own termios after the read returns EINTR,
or set the mode again immediately before each `read()` rather than once
before the loop. Worth checking against #150's `EINTR` retry, which is
the loop this would sit inside, and against `readinput()`, which reads
lines and wants canonical mode -- so it is only the keystroke reader
that needs this.
EOF
)"

}

3. resize the terminal to 90x26 **while the game is stopped**
4. `fg`

The top and bottom rules are redrawn to the new width but lose their
corner characters, and every interior row of the Status panel ends
without its border -- the whole rightmost screen column is unpainted.
The next output repaints it and the frame is whole again.

## Why it matters

Cosmetic and self-healing: one keystroke puts it right, and nothing is
lost. It is worth filing because it is a visible frame defect on a
gesture that is otherwise well covered -- the resize path has had a lot
of work (#163, #164, #166, #168) and both manuals promise the panels
follow the terminal -- and because a player who sees it has no way to
know it will heal.

The likely shape: curses' SIGTSTP handler does its own `reset_prog_mode()`
and refresh on resume, from a screen size it recorded before the stop,
and the resize that happened in between is applied to some of the frame
and not all of it. That is a guess from the symptom, not a measurement.

## Scope: pre-existing, and not caused by #158

Reproduced identically on a build of `main`, on the **first-init** path
(a game that came up full-screen straight away), which the #158 branch
does not touch.

That branch does make it reachable on one more path -- a game that fell
back, then came up full-screen at the play-again retry -- but only
because it restores curses' suspend handling there, which is the whole
point of the change: the retry path now behaves like the first-init one,
including in this.

## Where it was found

By `ui-review` on the branch for #158, while checking that the retry and
first-init suspend paths had been made consistent with each other. They
have; this is what they are consistently doing.

## How to see it

In a real terminal, or tmux:

```sh
tmux -f /dev/null -L t new-session -x 100 -y 30 'bash --norc --noprofile -i'
# inside: ./build/debug/sst -t tournament 7 short novice pw
# at COMMAND>, press Ctrl-Z
tmux -f /dev/null -L t resize-window -x 90 -y 26
# fg
```

Compare the rightmost column against the same journey with no resize
while stopped.
EOF

content.text:
Verifier is running. Where **#158** stands:

**The disputed fact is settled.** The issue couldn't tell whether plain mode hung too, because the earlier measurement used a `pgrep` pattern that matched more than one process. With exact PIDs: plain has no handlers at all (`SigCgt 0`) and recovers; the fallback game carries curses' `SIGTSTP` and hangs; panels-up recovers because it's curses' terminal to drive. So the asymmetry is real, and the fix is #152's save/restore widened to `SIGTSTP`.

**I also corrected the issue's hypothesis.** It guessed the damage happens on *resume* via `reset_prog_mode()`. Measured, the process never stops at all — the tty flips the moment `SIGTSTP` arrives. The conclusion held; the mechanism didn't.

**`ui-review` caught a blocker I introduced**, and it's the interesting one: my restore was *one-way* where the `SIGWINCH` restore beside it is two-way. Handing `SIGTSTP` back on the give-up path is right, but curses installs its handler once — so after a fallback → grow → play-again retry, the full-screen game came up with no suspend handling, and Ctrl-Z scribbled the shell's job message across the live panels. Fixed by mirroring the `cursewinch` mechanism that was already sitting in the same function.

Worth noting the arm for that needed an interactive shell in the pane: I checked the reviewer's suggested assertion and it doesn't discriminate — during the stop both builds look the same, and direct signals can't see it at all, because without a shell nothing writes over the panels.

Filed **#190** and **#191**, both reproduced on `main`.

`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c:1692-1695`, repeated in the `suspend` arm's comment in `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tests/tui.sh`:

That measurement was taken in a `start()`-style tmux pane. Under real job control — an interactive shell in the pane, game in its own pgrp (`pgid 473438`, `sid 473435`) — main's fallback game behaves the other way round:

```
[MAIN] SigCgt=0000000000084002 state=S+ tty=icanon echo
[MAIN] after TSTP: state=T tty=icanon echo        <- it does stop; tty untouched
[MAIN] tty forced canonical while stopped: icanon echo
[MAIN] after CONT:  state=R tty=-icanon -echo     <- the flip happens on resume
```

I forced the tty back to canonical *while stopped* and it flipped again after `SIGCONT`, so the resume itself is what reinstates curses' mode. 3/3 identical runs. So issue #158's original hypothesis (damage on resume) was right for a player at a shell prompt; the correction holds only where there is no job control. The same wording in the test comment ("measured, the process does not even stop") is wrong for the same reason.

The fix itself is unaffected and correct — restoring SIGTSTP prevents the damage whichever end it happens at. It is the stated mechanism, and the correction posted to the issue, that need retracting. Script: `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-scottdensmore-Developer-scottdensmore-super-star-trek/2ec84ddc-abc6-4082-9f37-fb6253a2c951/scratchpad/resume.sh`.

### 2. `start_shell()` truncates the developer's `~/.bash_history` — deterministic

`--norc --noprofile` does not turn history off. The pane's interactive bash loads `$HISTFILE` (default `~/.bash_history`) at startup and writes it back when it exits on the hangup from `cleanup`'s `kill-server`. With no rc file, `histappend` is off and `HISTFILESIZE` defaults to 500, so the file is **rewritten truncated to the last 500 lines**.

Measured through the real script, with a throwaway HOME holding 700 lines:

```
$ HOME=$F tests/tui.sh build/ci-debug/sst Debug
history before: 700
tui OK
history after: 500
```

499 of the 700 pre-existing entries survive; the test's own commands (`.../sst -t tournament 7 short novice pw`, `quit`, `n`, `y`, `fg`) are appended. This is the same class of harm `-L` and `-f /dev/null` exist to prevent, and it will already have happened to the real `~/.bash_history` on every run of this suite in this session (I did not read the user's history — that read was blocked, and I used a fake HOME instead). The lever is `HISTFILE`, not `--norc`.

**The `suspend` arm never actually suspends the fixed game.** By the mechanism in finding 1, `kill -TSTP` in a `start()` pane is discarded on the fixed build — measured `ps -o stat=` is `S+`, never `T`. The arm therefore asserts "the tty was not wrecked", not "the game stops and resumes". It does discriminate against `main` (I reproduced the hang: main answers nothing after TSTP/CONT), so it is not a blind test — but its blind spot is demonstrable. A second mutant that sets `SIGTSTP` to `SIG_IGN` on the give-up paths instead of restoring:

```
[MUT2-IGN] state after TSTP: S+   RESULT: game answered srscan after suspend/resume   <- arm passes
[MUT2-IGN] real C-z: state=S+ at +1..+5s, no "Stopped"                                <- player cannot suspend at all
```

A game a player cannot suspend passes this arm. The player journey #158 is actually about — fallback game, real Ctrl-Z, real `fg` — has no arm; `start_shell()` now makes one cheap. I ran it by hand: branch answers after C-z/fg, main hangs.

**Minor, `osx.c:61-62`:** "this code -- which runs only where the game fell back to the classic display" — the stdio `getch()` path runs whenever `!tui_active`, which includes a plain game started without `-t`. The same comment says "plain mode does the same" nine lines later. The conclusion still holds (a plain game's SigCgt is 0); the parenthetical does not.

---

**`osx.c` is comment-only, confirmed mechanically.** `gcc -E -P` output is byte-identical to `main`'s, and `gcc -S -O2 -g0` assembly is identical modulo the `.file` directive. Nothing about its behaviour moved.

**`start_shell()` leaves no process behind, and does not need the `stopped_pid` guard.** I reproduced the failure window you were worried about — C-z the game, then run the script's `cleanup` with the game in state `T` — and got `OK: no leftover game process after cleanup`, `OK: pane shell gone`. bash resends SIGHUP *and* SIGCONT to stopped jobs when it takes the hangup from `kill-server`, so a job stranded between C-z and `fg` is reaped by the next `cleanup` or by `finish()`. | #190 (pause survives suspend, space swallowed, Enter advances) | ✓ reproduced |
| panels-up suspend/resume unchanged | ✓ 80x24 and 72x24, branch identical to main |
| plain mode unchanged | ✓ `tournament 7` scripted journey byte-identical to main, and Debug == Release |

cmake --preset ci-release && cmake --build --preset ci-release --target clean && cmake --build --preset ci-release   # clean rebuilds, zero warnings under -Werror

Saving rather than forcing `SIG_DFL` is also what makes the `SIG_IGN`-at-startup case (a game launched with SIGTSTP ignored, where ncurses' `CatchIfDefault` installs nothing) a no-op in both directions. Every other multi-level arm in the file indents (compare `tests/tui.sh:4172-4215`). It is the one place in a 4900-line file where the nesting depth is invisible, which is where a later edit attaches a branch to the wrong `if`.

input.command:
gh issue create --title "slept_drag()'s comment says tm kill-server cannot reap a stopped process; on Linux it does" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

`tests/tui.sh`'s `slept_drag()` helper registers the process it stops in
`stopped_pid` so `finish()` can `SIGCONT` it, and explains why:

> Recorded so finish() can let it go again. tm kill-server hangs up the
> pane, and a SIGSTOPped process never acts on SIGHUP, so an interrupt
> inside this window would orphan the game still stopped -- silently,
> since the directory it played in is gone by then.

Measured on Linux, that does not happen. `tm kill-server` reaps the
stopped game every time:

| case | after `tm kill-server` |
| --- | --- |
| `kill -STOP` on a game in a `start()` pane | gone |
| real Ctrl-Z in a job-control pane, run 1 | gone |
| run 2 | gone |
| run 3 | gone |

The reason is POSIX's orphaned-process-group rule: when the session
leader exits and leaves a process group orphaned with a stopped member,
the kernel sends `SIGHUP` **followed by `SIGCONT`** to that group. The
stopped process is continued and then dies of the hangup. The comment's
premise -- "a SIGSTOPped process never acts on SIGHUP" -- is true in
isolation and beside the point, because the SIGCONT arrives with it.

## Why it matters

The guard itself is worth keeping: it costs a line, and this was

**State reviewed:** branch `fix/restore-sigtstp-on-fallback` at `1c256478b41c44f8a032f6f12e1a4e4252d6edb5` (identical to `main`, so `git diff main...HEAD` is empty and the whole change is unstaged). Four modified files: `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c` (save/restore SIGTSTP across both give-up paths, re-apply curses' handler on the success path), `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/sst.c` and `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/osx.c` (comment corrections only), `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tests/tui.sh` (`start_shell()`, a bash guard, `has_quadtitle()` split, two new suspend arms).

- `git diff --check` flags the added `sst.c` lines, but the whole file is CRLF on `main`; the new lines match the file. Not a finding.
- The three `slept_drag()` callers (`tests/tui.sh:1167`, `:1212`) both precede the new arms at `:3439` and `:3546`, and `startdir` is back to `$srcdir` at `:3377`. The `stopped_pid` sharing is safe.
- The existing SigCgt arm at `tests/tui.sh:3928` reads bit 27 only, so this branch does not break it.

## Findings

### should-fix

**1. `tests/tui.sh:3468` — the comment says "the four answers"; the line sends five.**

`tm send-keys ... 'tournament 7 short novice pw'` at `tests/tui.sh:3486` answers five prompts, all of them reached in `choose()` in `setup.c`: game type (`setup.c:467`), tournament number (`setup.c:471`), length and skill (`setup.c:522-523`), password (`setup.c:527`). A reader who counts finds five and then has to re-derive the rest of the note. This is the class `AGENTS.md` step 4 singles out, and the repo already carries a commit (#179) for exactly it. One-word fix: "the five answers".

**2. `tui.c:1811` — the oversize-pin give-up path's SIGTSTP restore has no test, and the cheap machinery for one is already in the file.**

You resolved this rather than fixed it, on a hand measurement of `SigCgt 0x4002`. That settles correctness today; it leaves no regression protection. `tui.c:1786` and `tui.c:1811` are the same line on two paths — delete the second and a player with `COLUMNS=190` in a 100-column terminal falls back and cannot suspend and resume, which is precisely the defect this branch exists to fix, and nothing in the suite fails. Generalising it to take the bit as a parameter (bit 19 for SIGTSTP alongside bit 27) and adding a fourth arm to the loop at `tests/tui.sh:3941` costs a handful of lines and no new journey. The arm-spec string is colon-separated and an `env COLUMNS=190` prefix contains no colon, so it drops into a sixth field cleanly. That would pin all four dispositions — fallback-by-floor, fallback-by-pin, plain, full-screen — against the mask rather than against a screen.

If you still prefer to resolve it, say so with that reasoning answered; it is a legitimate answer, but the resolution recorded so far only addresses whether the line is right now.

### nit

**3. `tests/tui.sh:3499-3504` — `has_quadtitle` is polled twice, and on the failure path that is four seconds of re-polling for nothing.**

`want_quadtitle` at `:3499` already ran the poll to exhaustion; `has_quadtitle` at `:3504` runs it again. Collapsing them says the same thing in one poll and removes the (harmless but odd) window where the arm both fails and clears the registration:

```sh
if has_quadtitle; then
        stopped_pid=
else
        fail "retry suspend: fg did not repaint the panels"
        dump
fi
```

The comment about clearing only after confirmation applies unchanged.

**4. `tests/tui.sh:26-30` — the header's requirements list does not mention the new hard bash dependency.**

The header documents the usage, the 77-on-no-tmux behaviour and the sub-second `sleep` requirement. `tests/tui.sh:614` now exits 1 with no tests run when bash is absent — a stronger requirement than either of those, and the one place a reader looks for it says nothing. One line beside the `sleep` note.

The diff plainly reaches the player: a fallback game becomes suspendable and resumable at all, and a retried full-screen game repaints after `fg`. `ui-review` was owed and you say it ran twice and bound both times, verdict acceptable-as-is on round 2.

I could not check the coverage list against the diff, because you place it "in the commit body and PR" and neither exists yet — nothing is committed on this branch and `gh pr list` shows no PR for it. What I can weigh instead is corroboration inside the diff, and it is unusually good: `tui.c:1353-1360` and `tests/tui.sh:3425-3430` both attribute the success-path re-apply to a `ui-review` finding, with a screen-level observation ("after `fg` the panels came back on one and not the other") that only a pass reading screens produces, on exactly the journey the diff's player-facing surface consists of. That is a run whose named coverage the change can reach, which is the test I am asked to apply.

Your three post-`ui-review` edits are all confined to `tests/tui.sh` — one comment and two `stopped_pid` clearing points — and none of them can alter what the game shows, so no rerun is owed. I take that from your account; with everything uncommitted there is no earlier state to diff against, so I could not verify it independently. Reproduce the round-2 coverage list in the commit body as you intend, since that is where the next reader will look for it.

`verifier` (four runs, last three PASS) and the mutation proofs on out-of-tree copies are outside what I can re-run here and I did not attempt to.

Issues #190, #191 and #192 are all open on the tracker and match what the comments at `osx.c:70`, `tests/tui.sh:3569` cite. Step 9 is satisfied.

		# $1 is the pane's shell; sst is its child.
		# The game, not whatever else the pane's shell has going.

		gamepid=
		for c in $(pgrep -P "$1" 2>/dev/null); do
			case $(tr '\0' ' ' < "/proc/$c/cmdline" 2>/dev/null) in
			*sst*) gamepid=$c; break ;;
			esac
		done
		[ -n "$gamepid" ] || { echo "nopid"; return; }
		mask=$(awk '/^SigCgt:/ { print $2 }' "/proc/$gamepid/status" 2>/dev/null)

		awk -v m="$mask" 'BEGIN {
			n = 0
			for (i = 1; i <= length(m); i++) {

			# POSIX awk has no >> operator.
			for (i = 0; i < 27; i++) n = int(n / 2)

oversize-pin path's restore (`tui.c:1810`, leaving the floor path's at

tui OK
```

Zero failures, exit 0. The floor twin is covered: deleting *that* one
makes the fallback game report `SigCgt 0000000008004002` and the
`fallback:SIGWINCH` arm fails.

## Why it is invisible

#150's `EINTR` retries make a leftover SIGWINCH handler behaviourally
harmless -- the readers retry rather than treating the interrupted read
as end of input -- so no journey can see it. Only a signal-mask arm can,
and there is no pinned SIGWINCH arm.

belt to #150's braces: losing it costs nothing a player sees *today*,
and the day someone adds a `select()` or `poll()` to the classic path it
costs the thing #152 was filed for. `tui_init()`'s own comment makes
exactly that argument about what is "not a blanket immunity for whatever
is added to that path later".

suite's mask reader to take the signal's bit and gave the arm spec an

added a pinned SIGTSTP arm to close the same gap one signal over. Filed
rather than fixed there: the SIGWINCH restore is #152's and the branch
is scoped to SIGTSTP, so adding it would have been an unrelated fix in
an unrelated diff. It is a one-line change to a table that branch has
already reshaped, so it should be cheap for whoever takes it.

# Verdict: request changes

Small, mechanical findings — one should-fix and four nits. The substance of the branch is sound, and I verified the central claims independently rather than taking them on report.

**State reviewed**: branch `fix/restore-sigtstp-on-fallback` at `1c25647` (`main`), with all four files unstaged and nothing staged or untracked — `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c`, `osx.c`, `sst.c`, `tests/tui.sh`. `git diff main` is the whole change, confirmed.

## What I verified myself

Built a copy of the worktree outside the repository with `ci-debug` (`-Werror`): clean, no warnings from the new `oldtstp`/`havetstp`/`cursetstp`/`havecursetstp` code. `sh -n tests/tui.sh` passes; no shellcheck available.

Then I read `SigCgt` off four live games on my own tmux socket, which is the fact the whole branch turns on:

| arm | measured | arm's `want` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| fallback 40x10 `-t` | `0x4002` | SIGWINCH no, SIGTSTP no ✓ |
| full-screen 80x24 `-t` | `0x8084002` | SIGWINCH yes, SIGTSTP yes ✓ |
| pinned 100x30 `COLUMNS=190` | `0x4002` | SIGTSTP no ✓ |
| plain 40x10 | `0x0` | no ✓ |

`0x4002` is SIGINT (bit 1) and SIGTERM (bit 14) only, which is exactly what the rewritten `sst.c:853` comment now claims and what the old one got wrong. Bit 19 for SIGTSTP and bit 27 for SIGWINCH are right for Linux (`signum - 1`), and the block is `/proc`-guarded so no other numbering is in play.

I also built the mutant your finding 2 is about — deleting *only* the oversize-path `if (havetstp) sigaction(SIGTSTP, &oldtstp, NULL);` at `tui.c:1811` — and got `0x84002` for the pinned game, i.e. SIGTSTP caught where `no` is wanted. The new `pinned` arm does discriminate, and nothing else in the mask block would have caught it. The precondition string `LINES/COLUMNS make it` appears in the scrollback of that session, so the fallback assertion is real and not scenery.

The C is otherwise correct in context. `tui_init()` is only re-entered from `sst.c:691` under `usetui && !tui_active`, and `tui_active` is cleared only by `tui_shutdown()` at exit — so there is no path where a successful full-screen game is followed by a give-up that would hand the fallback game *curses'* SIGTSTP by restoring a stale `oldtstp`. The one-shot capture into `cursetstp` mirrors `cursewinch` exactly, both give-up paths restore, and the success-path re-apply sits before `cbreak()/noecho()` where it belongs. `osx.c` and `sst.c` are comment-only, so plain mode cannot have moved.

## Findings

### should-fix

**`tests/tui.sh:3897`** — the mask block's design rationale still says "Three arms, because two of them cannot tell each other apart", and the loop below it now has seven.

The diff updated `sigwinch_caught()` → `sig_caught()` inside that very sentence and left the count. That paragraph is the block's specification — it is where the next person reads *why* the arms are arranged as they are — and it now describes a loop that no longer exists. This is the class AGENTS.md step 4 singles out: a sentence stating a number that a later change quietly falsifies, in text written to answer an earlier round about exactly this. `sig_caught()`'s own comment explains the SIGTSTP triple and the pinned arm, but the "two cannot tell each other apart, the third is the discriminator" argument is what someone adding an eighth arm needs, and it is stranded.

Suggested fix: restate it without a literal count — e.g. that each signal gets a fallback/plain pair which cannot tell each other apart, plus a full-screen arm that expects "yes" and is the one that fails if the reading itself breaks; and that the pinned arm covers the second give-up path where SIGTSTP has no journey. Written that way, adding the `pinned:...:SIGWINCH:27:` row from #193 later will not falsify it again.

Same paragraph, two adjacent instances of the same slip, cheap to fold into one edit:

- **`tests/tui.sh:3893`** — "SIGWINCH is 28 -- so bit 27" is now half the story; SIGTSTP/20/bit 19 is the other half and appears only 25 lines further down.
- **`tests/tui.sh:3913`, `3915`, `3919`** — the guard messages still read `sigwinch: no readable /proc on Linux CI, so the disposition went unchecked`, `note: no /proc, so the SIGWINCH disposition went unchecked`, and `sigwinch: pgrep is missing`. These three gate all seven arms. Concrete failure: `/proc` goes unreadable on Linux CI, the log says SIGWINCH went unchecked, and the reader has no idea the four SIGTSTP arms — the point of this branch — were the bigger loss. This is the same regression you already fixed for the per-arm messages after the verifier flagged it; these are outside the loop so `$sig` is not in scope, but the words can still name both signals.

### nit

**`tests/tui.sh:114`** — `finish()`'s comment says "Let any process `slept_drag()` stopped go again". Two new arms now write `stopped_pid` too (`3497`, `3579`). Name them, or drop the attribution to `slept_drag()`.

**`tests/tui.sh:3497`, `3509`, `3579`, `3602`** — `stopped_pid` is left set on every failure path in the two new arms, where `slept_drag()` clears it on all four of its own exits. If `wait_for 'Stopped'` fails, or `has_quadtitle` fails after `fg`, or the `UNRECOGNIZED COMMAND` expect fails, the variable survives to the EXIT trap ~150 seconds and a dozen `cleanup` calls later. The next arm's `kill-server` has reaped the game by then (your own comment at `3570` measures this on Linux), so `finish()`'s `kill -CONT` goes to a dead — or recycled — pid on a shared machine. Harmless in the ordinary case, but it is the same "do not touch a pid you did not create" reasoning that `-L` exists for. Suggest clearing `stopped_pid=` in each failure branch, so the registration never outlives the window it insures.

**`tests/tui.sh:3492`** — `if ! to_command || ! has_quadtitle` fails with "the panels never came up on the retry" for both causes, so a second game that never reached a prompt at all is reported as a panel problem. The comment six lines above is expressly worried about a CI log sending the reader to the wrong line; this is the same shape one level up. Suggest splitting the two, or wording it "the retry never reached a prompt with panels".

**`CMakeLists.txt:94`, `101`** — the comment still says "far above the ~11s it takes to pass" against a measured 202.6s and `TIMEOUT 300`, i.e. 1.48x headroom on a test this branch adds two ~25s journey arms to. The stale comment is #101's and you have updated it there; the *headroom* is what this branch narrows, and a loaded macOS runner is the case that bites. Either raise the timeout here (it is arguably in-slice, since this branch is what consumes the margin) or add the headroom observation to #101 alongside the 202.6s figure.

## On the two things you asked about

**#193 — I do not dispute it.** `tui.c:1810`'s SIGWINCH restore is #152's line and untouched by this diff; the existing three SIGWINCH arms use 40x10 and 80x24 only, so I confirm the oversize path's SIGWINCH restore has no coverage and never did. Step 9's rule is exactly on point and filing is the right answer, one-line fix or not. One consequence: if #193 lands as that extra row, the block comment gets falsified again — which is the argument for fixing the should-fix above by removing the count rather than changing "three" to "seven".

**Review coverage.** You named all three passes, and the diff corroborates the `ui-review` claim in a way I could check rather than take on trust: `tui.c:1513-1521` and `tests/tui.sh:3429-3432` both record round 1 finding the missing success-path re-apply, with the `0x8004002` / `0x8084002` pair — that is a journey this change plainly reaches, and it produced a code change. For round 2 you gave the verdict but not the list of what it exercised, which is the half I am meant to check against the diff. I am satisfied here without it, because every edit made after round 2 (the four findings above plus the `$sig` message fix) lives in `tests/tui.sh` or in comments, so the game code round 2 saw is byte-for-byte what is being committed. Put the list in the commit body as you planned; I would expect it to name the fallback game's Ctrl-Z/fg at `COMMAND>`, the retry path's panels after `fg`, and the pinned refusal — anything narrower than those would be worth a second look.

## Not reviewed

I did not run the `tui` test, the golden battery, or the `ci-release` preset — that is the verifier's scope and it reported PASS four times, including independent rebuilds of both mutants. I built `ci-debug` only, to check the new declarations against `-Werror`. I could not verify the macOS half of anything (`ps -o comm=`, `bash` presence, the kill-server-reaps-a-stopped-game claim at `tests/tui.sh:3570`, which the comment itself scopes to Linux). The `#190` claim in `osx.c:70-73` — that the space bar is swallowed until Enter after a resume at a pause, and that plain mode does the same — I took on your measurement; it is a filed issue and not this slice's to fix, and I agree with that call since plain mode's `getch()` has always set the terminal non-canonical around its own `read()`.

The next arm's `kill-server` has reaped the game by then (your own comment at `3570` measures this on Linux), so `finish()`'s `kill -CONT` goes to a dead — or recycled — pid on a shared machine. **`tests/tui.sh:3492`** — `if ! to_command || ! has_quadtitle` fails with "the panels never came up on the retry" for both causes, so a second game that never reached a prompt at all is reported as a panel problem. Verifier is on the final state. One correction worth making to something I told you earlier, because the reviewer's evidence changed it:

I said the `stopped_pid` registration prevents an orphaned stopped game. The verifier measured that on Linux `kill-server` reaps it anyway — the orphaned-process-group rule sends SIGHUP *and* SIGCONT. So the guard is insurance for macOS, which nobody has checked, not a fix for something observed. I'd copied that reasoning from `slept_drag()`'s comment on `main` rather than measuring it, which is how the same wrong sentence ended up needing to be caught twice. That's filed as **#192**.

The other thing I'd flag from this branch: the reviewers repeatedly found I had the relevant fact *already*, written in the tree, often in the file I was editing. The unanchored `' Quadrant '` search sits twenty lines from the comment warning against it. The `timeout(1)`-on-macOS problem is stated in `CMakeLists.txt` and guarded in five test scripts. The `~/.bash_history` damage is the same class as the `tmux kill-server` incident AGENTS.md opens with. In each case I read past it.

**Filed this branch:** #190, #191, #192, #193, plus fresh measurements on #101.

<result>## Verdict

**Pass** — every check ran and everything is green. Two non-blocking findings, both in `tests/tui.sh` and both about the item-5/item-6 rework you asked me to look at. No failures, no flakes, no environment gaps.

## Failures

None. Both configurations, full suite, 12/12:

```
ctest --preset ci-debug    → 100% tests passed, 0 failed out of 12  (384.93 s)
ctest --preset ci-release  → 100% tests passed, 0 failed out of 12  (376.86 s)
```

`analyze` **Passed** (36.82 s Debug / 37.97 s Release) — it ran, it did not SKIP, so `gcc -fanalyzer` (gcc 15.2.0) really covered the sources at the depth #173 set. Both `ci-*` builds were done with `--clean-first`, so every translation unit was recompiled with `-Werror`: zero warnings, zero diagnostics.

## `tui` runtime (re-measured, as asked)

| Config | runs | TIMEOUT | headroom |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ci-debug | 202.59 s, 202.59 s, 202.63 s | 300 | 32% |
| ci-release | 193.62 s, 193.95 s | 300 | 35% |

Identical to the 202.6 s you had. The added branch and comments cost nothing measurable, and the spread across three Debug runs is 0.04 s — this is not a test near its limit.

## Findings (the two arms)

I rebuilt the question you asked as an experiment rather than a read: a copy of the tree outside the repository, with `tests/tui.sh` trimmed to the preamble plus just the two suspend arms, and a mutant of that trim with `tm send-keys ... 'fg' Enter` replaced by `:` — i.e. the resume genuinely never happens.

**What holds.** The mutant fails exactly and only the two intended messages (`retry suspend: fg did not repaint the panels`, `suspend: the game stopped answering after a suspend and resume`), so the split in item 6 reports the right cause and the arms assert what their comments claim. I also independently reproduced both of your mutation claims, building each variant in the copy with `cmake --preset ci-debug`:

- `main`'s `tui.c` → only `suspend: the game stopped answering after a suspend and resume` fails; the retry arm correctly passes (on `main` curses' handler was never disturbed).
- branch `tui.c` with the success-path re-apply deleted → only `retry suspend: fg did not repaint the panels` fails.

**What leaks: nothing, on Linux.** Sampling `ps` twice a second through the mutant run, the game sits in `T` for ~8 s in each arm while the arm fails — so those failure paths really do run with the game stopped — and after the script exits there is no `sst` process and no stopped process at all, in two runs. `cleanup`'s `tm kill-server` reaps it, exactly as the arm's comment records.

### 1. The failure paths clear `stopped_pid` without resuming first (should-fix)

All four new clears (`tests/tui.sh:3507`, `:3519`, `:3591`, `:3614`) drop the registration bare. `slept_drag()` does not: every one of its failure exits is `kill -CONT "$1"; stopped_pid=` (`:214-215`, `:228`, `:232`). So item 5 traded a stale registration for a dropped rescue — on those paths the game is stopped, `finish()` has nothing left to CONT, and the only thing that resumes it is `kill-server`'s SIGHUP+SIGCONT, which the arm's own comment at `:3579-3584` is careful to say was measured on Linux and that macOS is the other platform CI runs. A `kill -CONT "$stopped_pid" 2>/dev/null` before each clear gets both properties for one line and makes the two helpers say the same thing.

### 2. The retry arm's comment is falsified by the branch two lines under it (nit, but the AGENTS.md kind)

`tests/tui.sh:3510-3513`:

```
# One poll, and the registration cleared
# only once the resume is confirmed: an fg
# that did not take would otherwise drop it
# with the game still stopped.
```

`:3516-3519` clears it precisely when the resume was *not* confirmed. The sibling arm's comment (`:3608-3613`) states the real rule and is correct; this one reads as a claim about behavior the code does not have. Reword, or fix per finding 1 and let the comment stand.

## Missing coverage

Nothing new in the diff is uncovered. For the record on what I checked beyond the arms:

- `osx.c` and `sst.c` are **comment-only**: `gcc -fpreprocessed -dD -E -P` output on each is byte-identical to `main`'s. So the risk in those two files is claim accuracy, not behavior — and I measured every claim (below); they hold.
- All `tui_init()` exits are symmetric: the two pre-`initscr()` returns (`tui.c:1644`, `:1646`) need no restore, and both give-up returns restore SIGWINCH and SIGTSTP (`:1785-1786`, `:1810-1811`). The success path re-applies both (`:1820-1823`).
- I looked for a hole the mask arms could not see — a state with the *classic stdio* reader and curses' SIGTSTP handler still installed — by driving two retry sequences by hand: (a) full-screen 100x30 → quit → shrink to 70x20 → play again; (b) 70x20 fallback → grow to 100x30 → play again (panels up) → quit → shrink to 70x20 → play again. In both, the game stays curses-driven with the panels turned down (`tty -icanon`, SigCgt `0x8084002`), `tui_init()` is not re-entered from a curses-up state, and C-z/fg/`zzz` answers normally. So no such state is reachable and the fix is complete for the paths that exist. Worth knowing that this "panels turned down by a shrink" state has no *suspend* arm anywhere in the file — it works today, it predates this branch, and it is not this slice's; mentioning it only so the gap is on the record.
- #193 (SIGWINCH on the oversize give-up path) remains uncovered, as filed and resolved. The SIGTSTP half of that path *is* covered, by the `pinned` mask arm — and I confirmed it directly: that game's SigCgt is `0x4002`.

## Environment issues

None. tmux, bash, pgrep, `/proc` and gcc 15.2.0 all present; the `analyze`, `tui` guards all ran rather than skipping. `cppcheck`, `clang-tidy` and `scan-build` are not installed — bonus only, per the brief, and `analyze` is what step 2 rests on.

## What ran

- `cmake --preset ci-debug` + `cmake --build --preset ci-debug --clean-first`; same for `ci-release`. Zero warnings under `-Werror`.
- `ctest --preset ci-debug`, `ctest --preset ci-release` — full suites, one pass each.
- `ctest --preset ci-debug -R '^tui$'` ×2, `ctest --preset ci-release -R '^tui$'` ×1 — flake and runtime sampling.
- Journeys against `./build/ci-debug/sst` (and the plain one against `ci-release` too): piped `regular/short/novice/xyz/srscan/status/quit/n` in both builds, exit 0; TUI at 80x24 and 72x24 — panels, `status`, quit-to-exit with `GAMEEXIT=0`; real C-z/fg from an interactive bash pane for the fallback 70x20 game, the plain game and the full-screen game (all three suspend, resume and answer the next command); the two shrink/grow retry sequences above.
- Signal-mask measurements via `/proc/<pid>/status` decoded to names: fallback `0x4002` (SIGINT, SIGTERM only), plain `0x0`, full-screen `0x8084002`, pinned-oversize give-up `0x4002` — these confirm the rewritten comments in `sst.c:853-`, `osx.c:57-` and `tui.c:1687-1721`.
- Mutation re-proofs on copies outside the repository at `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-scottdensmore-Developer-scottdensmore-super-star-trek/2ec84ddc-abc6-4082-9f37-fb6253a2c951/scratchpad/copy` (tracked files only, built there with `cmake --preset ci-debug`): `main`'s `tui.c`; branch minus the success-path re-apply; and a `tui.sh` mutant with `fg` never sent.

The repository is untouched: `git status --porcelain` is the same four modified files, and I removed only the tmux socket files my own probes left in `/tmp/tmux-1000`, each on its own `-L` socket, never a bare `kill-server`.</result>

git add -A && git commit -F - <<'EOF'
fix(tui): let a fallback game be suspended and resumed

initscr() installs handlers for SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGTSTP, and
endwin() takes none of them away. #152 restored SIGWINCH on the give-up
path for that reason; SIGTSTP is the one left that costs a player
something. A game that fell back to the classic display reads with the
stdio reader, which wants the terminal in canonical mode, and curses'
handler put it into curses' program mode instead on the resume. The
game never answered again and had to be killed from another terminal.

#158 asked for a disputed fact to be settled before anything was built:
whether plain mode hangs too. Settled with exact pids, the earlier
measurement having used a pgrep pattern that matched more than one
process. Plain mode installs no handlers at all (SigCgt 0) and recovers;
the fallback game is 0x84002 and hangs; a game whose panels are up is
0x8084002 and recovers, being curses' terminal to drive. So the
asymmetry is real and the fix is #152's two lines widened.

Curses installs its handler once and a second initscr() does not
reinstall it, so the give-up restore alone would have cost the retry
#154 exists for: fall back, grow the terminal, say yes at play-again,
and the panels come up with no suspend handling -- a Ctrl-Z printing
the shell's job message over them and fg never repainting. So the
cursewinch mechanism is mirrored with a cursetstp, captured after
initscr() and re-applied on the success path.

SIGINT and SIGTERM are left alone: measured, a fallback game exits 1 on
Ctrl-C where a plain one exits 130, which reaches a shell script and
nothing a player sees.

Comments in sst.c and osx.c said the fallback game catches SIGTSTP and
that curses' handler carries SA_RESTART. Both halves are now false, and
they are a matched pair -- updating one and not the other would leave
the two files contradicting each other about the same signal on the
same path.

tests/tui.sh gains two suspend journeys and four signal-mask arms. The
journeys need job control, so start_shell() runs the game from an
interactive bash; it sets HISTFILE and INPUTRC to /dev/null, because
--norc does not stop bash rewriting the developer's ~/.bash_history
capped at 500 lines, which it had already done to a real one before the
verifier caught it. The mask arms generalise the existing SIGWINCH
reader to take the signal's bit, which covers the second give-up path
at 0.25s where a second suspend journey would have cost 25.

Each arm is mutation-proved with the break named beside it: main's
tui.c fails the suspend journey and two mask arms; SIGTSTP set to
SIG_IGN on the give-up paths fails the journey with "C-z did not
suspend", a game a player cannot suspend at all having passed the
arm's first version; deleting the success-path re-apply fails the retry
journey; deleting only the oversize path's restore fails the pinned
mask arm.

Plain mode is unchanged: a piped tournament journey is byte-identical.

ui-review ran twice and bound both; verifier six times; code-review
seven. Issues filed: #190, #191, #192, #193. Measurements added to #101.

Closes #158

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

gh pr create --base main --head fix/restore-sigtstp-on-fallback --title "fix(tui): let a fallback game be suspended and resumed" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Closes #158.

## What was wrong

`initscr()` installs handlers for SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGTSTP; `endwin()`
takes none away. #152 restored SIGWINCH on the give-up path for that
reason. SIGTSTP is the one left that costs a player something: a game
that fell back to the classic display reads with the stdio reader, which
wants canonical mode, and curses' handler put the terminal into curses'
*program* mode on the resume. The game never answered again and had to
be killed from another terminal.

## The disputed fact, settled first

#158 asked for that before anything was built — its second reproduction
had **both** modes hanging, from a `pgrep` pattern that matched more than
one process. Measured with exact pids:

| case | `SigCgt` | tty before | tty after resume | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| plain (no `-t`) | `0` | canonical | canonical | recovers |
| `-t` fallen back | `0x84002` | canonical | **raw** | **hangs** |
| `-t` panels up | `0x8084002` | raw | raw | recovers |

I also corrected the issue's mechanism *and then had my correction
corrected*: I claimed the process never stops and the tty flips at signal
time, which was an artifact of measuring in a pane where the game shares
the pane shell's orphaned process group, so the kernel discards the stop.
Under real job control the game stops and the damage is on the resume —
the issue's original hypothesis. The comments say so.

## The fix

Save and restore SIGTSTP on both give-up paths. Because curses installs
its handler once and a second `initscr()` does not reinstall it, that
alone would have cost the retry #154 exists for — fall back, grow the
terminal, say yes at play-again, and the panels come up with **no**
suspend handling, so Ctrl-Z prints the shell's job message over them and
`fg` never repaints. So the existing `cursewinch` mechanism is mirrored
with a `cursetstp`, captured after `initscr()` and re-applied on the
success path.

SIGINT and SIGTERM are left alone: measured, a fallback game exits 1 on
Ctrl-C where a plain one exits 130 — a shell script's problem, not a
player's.

## Tests

Two suspend journeys and four signal-mask arms, each mutation-proved
with the break named beside the assertion:

| break | fails |
| --- | --- |
| `main`'s `tui.c` | the suspend journey **and** two mask arms |
| SIGTSTP set to `SIG_IGN` on the give-up paths | `suspend: C-z did not suspend the fallback game` |
| success-path re-apply deleted | `retry suspend: fg did not repaint the panels` |
| **only** the oversize path's restore deleted | `SIGTSTP: the pinned game's handler is 'yes'` |

That third row is the one worth noting. I twice **resolved** "the
pinned-size path has no suspend arm" on cost grounds; `code-review`
accepted the cost argument but pointed out the resolution only
established the line was right *now*, and supplied a mechanism I had not
considered — the suite already reads `SigCgt` and tests one bit, so
generalising that reader covers the path at **0.25s** instead of the 25s
a second journey would cost. The fourth row is now possible because of it.

The `SIG_IGN` row is the other one: a game a player cannot suspend *at
all* passed the first version of that arm, because in a `start()` pane
the game's process group is orphaned and the kernel discards the stop —
so the arm was asserting "the tty was not wrecked", not "the game
suspends". It now uses real Ctrl-Z and `fg` through an interactive shell.

Plain mode is byte-identical to the pre-change build.

## A warning about the test helper

`start_shell()` puts an interactive bash in the pane for job control.
`--norc` does **not** disable history: bash reads `$HISTFILE` at startup
and rewrites it capped at 500 lines on exit. **It truncated the
developer's real `~/.bash_history` before the verifier caught it.** It
now sets `HISTFILE=/dev/null INPUTRC=/dev/null`, verified by strace to
open nothing under `$HOME` and by a 700-line throwaway history that comes
back 700. Same class as the `tmux kill-server` incident AGENTS.md opens
with, and worth knowing before anyone else puts a shell in a pane.

## Resolved rather than fixed

- **#193** — the oversize path's *SIGWINCH* restore has no coverage at
  all; deleting it passes the whole suite, because #150's `EINTR` retries
  make a leftover SIGWINCH handler behaviourally invisible. That is
  #152's line, so it is filed rather than folded in, even though the new
  spec makes it a one-row change.
- **#192** — `slept_drag()`'s comment on `main` says `kill-server` cannot
  reap a stopped process. Measured on Linux, it does. I had copied that
  reasoning into my own arms instead of measuring it.

## Review passes

`ui-review` twice, `verifier` six times, `code-review` seven. Round 1 of
`ui-review` found the missing `cursetstp` mirror. `verifier` found the
history truncation, the harness artifact behind my wrong mechanism, and
that the first suspend arm never suspended anything. `code-review` found
that neither arm asserted the fallback precondition, that I had used an
unanchored `' Quadrant '` search twenty lines from the comment warning
against it, that I had updated one half of a matched comment pair, and —
after I "fixed" a stale registration — that I had traded it for a dropped
rescue, where `slept_drag()` in the same file does both.

**`ui-review` round 2 verdict: acceptable as-is.** Coverage: the retry
journey at 70x20→100x30 with `SigCgt` at each stage; the same at 72x24;
the same with a `help move` pause open at the moment of suspend; fallback
suspend/resume at `COMMAND>`; fallback via the oversize pin; two repeated
failed retries; suspend, resize *while stopped*, resume, then play again;
plain and first-init panels games as baselines; Ctrl-C in fallback versus
plain; and the full `tests/tui.sh`.

## Issues

Filed: **#190**, **#191**, **#192**, **#193**. Measurements added to
**#101** (`tui` now 202.6s of its 300s, with the per-arm split showing
journeys cost and mask checks are nearly free).

**The best outcome came from being argued out of a resolution.** I twice resolved "the pinned-size path has no suspend arm" on cost grounds. `code-review` granted the cost argument, then pointed out my resolution only established the line was correct *now* — and supplied a mechanism I hadn't considered, using the mask reader already in the file. Deleting only that restore now fails a specific arm, at 0.25s instead of 25. I'd been defending the cost of the one option I'd thought of, not answering the goal.

The recurring failure mode across all four branches was the same: the fact I needed was already written down in the tree — often in the file I was editing — and I reasoned past it. The unanchored `' Quadrant '` search sits twenty lines from the comment warning against it; `timeout(1)`-on-macOS is stated in `CMakeLists.txt` and guarded in five scripts; `slept_drag()` shows both halves of the resume-then-clear pattern I applied half of.
